meeting_header: Date: 2026-09-21 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 62m | Location: Zoom | Recording: Enabled\nAttendees: Maya Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Nina Cho (Redwood CSM), Rina Patel (Alderbridge - Head of ML), Marcus Yeo (Alderbridge - VP Eng), Samir Khan (Alderbridge - SRE), Leah Gomez (Alderbridge - Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros — we'll get into the runway numbers and then dig into the pilot scope.
[00:18] Rina (Head of ML): Hi, thanks. We wanted to get clarity on costs and what a Dedicated pilot would look like, especially for inference at peak. We're seeing some latency spikes during our morning batch windows.
[00:32] Maya: Got it. Ethan will cover the perf/architecture side. Nina will cover onboarding and ops.
[00:44] Ethan (SE): hey, hi all. quick note: we've read the summary you sent — the sample workload looks like a mix of short chat-like queries and longer summarization calls, so sequence lengths vary which affects batching.
[00:58] Marcus (VP Eng): yeah that's right. roughly 70% short q/a ~ <64 tokens and 30% longer ~ 512 tokens. spikes around 09:00-11:00 UTC.
[01:12] Ethan: okay that's helpful. for cost/latency tradeoffs we usually recommend prefix caching / KV cache for the long dialogs and aggressive batching for the short ones. that can reduce per-token cost but the latency tail depends on how you set target latency SLOs.
[01:33] Rina: when you say "KV cache" are we talking Redwood's prefix caching or something we need to manage?
[01:40] Maya: it's automatic on the runtime if you enable session caching. you can configure cache TTL and what to persist across requests. Ethan: correct.
[01:48] Ethan: yes, we handle the cache inside the inference runtime; customers don't have to run it. small correction — it's more like a K V layer for key/value activations; sometimes the transcriber writes K V as "K V" and it looks odd.
[02:00] Samir (SRE): latency tail is our concern.  p99 currently jumps to ~1.8s on longer calls which causes UX issues. what levers do we have?
[02:13] Ethan: options — 1) pin to Dedicated GPU pool for consistent throughput; 2) use a slightly smaller quantized variant for the long summaries to save tokens and speed, 3) tune batching window and priority routing so short requests get fast lanes.
[02:29] Leah (Product): small question on quality tradeoff with quantization — how big is the quality delta?
[02:36] Ethan: depends on model family. for some LLaMA-like weights, int8 Q or PTQ can be nearly identical for summarization but can degrade edge-case instruction-following; we can run the quant profile using your eval set.
[02:51] Rina: our success criteria for pilot is <200ms median for short calls and p95 under 400ms, and for long calls p95 under 1.2s ideally. is that realistic?
[03:04] Ethan: median 200ms for short calls is achievable on Dedicated with hot KV and batching, but p95 400ms is aggressive at your volume unless we do dedicated hot pools and some request shaping. we can get close on hosted with burst capacity but it's less predictable.
[03:20] Marcus: can you quantify cost delta between hosted burst vs dedicated reserved? we have finance looking for a 6-12 week pilot number.
[03:28] Maya: we'll send a two-path estimate: hosted pay-as-you-go with burst buffers and a Dedicated reserve with a month commit. the Dedicated option reduces unit costs at scale — we'll include both.
[03:40] Nina (CSM): operationally we'll include runbooks and dashboards. you'll get per-route token and latency breakdowns in Console.
[03:47] Samir: SSO and audit logs are must-haves. we need RBAC and SAML. also KMS integration for key management — we can't have unmanaged keys.
[03:59] Maya: understood. Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations (customer-managed) for Private deployments and Dedicated can be integrated with your KMS via the control plane. we'll attach the security playbook.
[04:12] Rina: do you have SOC2 or ISO certs? our compliance gate asks for that before we can run regulated PII.
[04:18] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; we'll share the attestation and the whitepaper on data residency and retention.
[04:26] Marcus: great. timeline question: we want to start pilot early October. what's realistic?
[04:33] Ethan: 2-3 weeks for Dedicated provisioning including networking and SAML if everything is green. baseline perf tests can run in parallel — we'll need your prompt set and a service account.
[04:44] Rina: we'll share a 500-example prompt set and the sampling of longer dialogs by Friday.
[04:50] Ethan: perfect. we'll run perf + quality benchmarks and return a spreadsheet with tokens, latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:58] Samir: about on-prem — we might need an air-gapped option for a subset of PII workloads. is that supported?
[05:05] Maya: yes, Redwood Private has on-prem packaging, but that is a separate procurement path — can be parallel but timing is longer, 6-8 weeks typically.
[05:16] Leah: one more — routing: can we route high priority traffic to Dedicated and low cost to hosted? we want a fallback if Dedicated is saturated.
[05:25] Ethan: yes, smart routing policy supports tiered routing by latency and cost policy. you can define canary and automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant.
[05:36] Rina: awesome. any pitfalls you usually see in pilots?
[05:40] Ethan: three things: 1) mismatch in traffic shape vs sample set, 2) poor caching TTL choices, 3) forgetting to pin model versions so evals are repeatable. we'll give a checklist.
[05:52] Nina: and we'll include success metrics template: cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99, error rate, and fallback counts.
[06:01] Marcus: let's talk numbers — show us a sample for 1 million tokens per day with 70/30 split short/long — can you give a ballpark now?
[06:10] Maya: ballpark only — hosted with burst: $X per 1M tokens, Dedicated reserve: ~0.7X per 1M tokens but requires commit. we'll fill in actuals in the deck.
[06:22] Rina: okay, good. next steps recap please.
[06:26] Maya: action items: we will share pilot pricing, security docs, and a perf baseline plan. Ethan will run tests when you share prompts. Rina will confirm data residency.
[06:37] Marcus: timeline — confirm by Friday and provision first week of October.
[06:42] Maya: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and the kickoff.
[06:49] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:52] Ethan: thanks, bye.
